nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study employs the CentileBrain normative model, which uses Multivariate Factorial Polynomial Regression (MFPR) to generate sex-specific normative models for subcortical volume estimation. MFPR was also applied to analyze age-related trajectories of harmonized subcortical volumes.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: The CentileBrain employs Multivariate Factorial Polynomial Regression (MFPR) algorithm which performs robustly on healthy subjects, generating sex-specific normative models for the volume estimation of subcortical regions

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Subcortical volumes of bilateral brain structures: Thalamus, Caudate, Putamen, Pallidum, Hippocampus, Amygdala, and Accumbens. These volumes were segmented using SynthSeg+ and SynthSeg-WMH from T1w and FLAIR MRI images.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: generating sex-specific normative models for the volume estimation of subcortical regions in both right and left brain hemispheres: Thalamus, Caudate, Putamen, Pallidum, Hippocampus, Amygdala, and Accumbens

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The CentileBrain model uses age and sex as covariates to estimate expected subcortical volumes for healthy subjects. ComBat-GAM harmonization was also applied accounting for age and sex to mitigate site effects.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: The CentileBrain model employs patient-specific age and sex covariates to estimate the subcortical volume of a healthy subject of such age and sex
